atherogenesis in cholesterol-fed animals is accompanied by changes in the chemical and physical properties of the arterial wall that are not necessarily related to the accumulation of lipid.
the composition of the arterial walls changes during the development of atherosclerosis and that these compositional changes may be related to the development of atherogenesis.

the composition of arterial lipids is not static, that the changes in composition are related to the changes in the morphology of the arterial wall, and that the changes in the composition and morphology of arterial lipids and lipoproteins are associated with the changes in the plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical composition of arterial tissue and the biochemical mechanisms that lead to the changes observed in aortic tissue in atherosclerosis.
the composition and metabolism in arterial tissue and in the plasma of the constituents of the arterial wall and of lipoproteins in the plasma.
the composition and metabolism in arterial tissue, and with the relationship of the composition and metabolism to the development of atherosclerosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
atherosclerosis is a degenerative disease of the arterial wall in which there is an accumulation of lipids, especially cholesterol and its esters, in the arterial wall.
the chemical composition of arterial tissues is not well understood and that there is little evidence to suggest that the chemical composition is the primary cause of atherosclerosis.
the composition and metabolism are not well enough understood to be useful in the understanding of the degenerative changes in arteries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
atherosclerosis is the consequence of a number of factors, including hyperlipidemia and hypercholesteremia.

the chemical and biochemical studies of aortic lipids have been useful in defining some of the early changes in the composition of the arterial tissue in experimental atherosclerosis and have suggested some of the mechanisms involved.

arterial tissue has the capability of accumulating esterified fatty acid and cholesterol, and the accumulation of these lipids is a consequence of a number of biochemical changes that occur in plasma, arterial tissue, and arterial wall cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
atherosclerosis is a complex disease that is influenced by a number of factors, including diet, genetics, and lifestyle.

the arterial wall is a highly active metabolic tissue and, in addition to the well-known changes in arterial wall composition, there are also changes in the rates of formation and utilization of the major classes of lipids in the arterial wall.
there is no simple relationship between plasma lipid concentrations and the composition of the arterial tissue.
